summary: This bill repeals the USA PATRIOT Act and restores every law it amended to the exact text in effect on October 25, 2001.

scores.thoughts: The bill repeals the USA PATRIOT Act but contains no provisions that directly authorize, increase, or decrease any government appropriations or programs. Any potential spending effects from eliminated surveillance activities are indirect and speculative.
The bill addresses only the repeal of the PATRIOT Act and has no provisions related to tax policy, rates, or revenue collection.
No provisions in the bill relate to healthcare delivery, insurance, public coverage, or market-based systems.
The bill does not address firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.

The PATRIOT Act contained Title IV provisions on border security and immigration enforcement. Repealing the Act would remove those post-2001 authorities and restore pre-2001 rules, producing a minor loosening of immigration enforcement tools.
The bill contains no language concerning reproductive rights or abortion access.
While the PATRIOT Act affected certain intelligence authorities, the bill makes no changes to military or defense appropriations or force structure.
No environmental or regulatory provisions appear in the bill.
The bill does not address welfare programs, food assistance, or entitlement spending.
No education policy, school funding, or choice provisions are present.
The bill does not modify drug enforcement statutes or decriminalization measures.

Repeal would eliminate several PATRIOT Act surveillance authorities used in criminal investigations, modestly shifting policy away from expanded law-enforcement tools toward pre-2001 limits on policing powers.
No trade, tariff, or globalization provisions are included.
The bill does not address deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
No provisions relate to LGBTQ legal protections or rights.
The bill makes no changes to foreign assistance programs.
No election administration, voting access, or integrity measures are addressed.

The sole purpose of the bill is to repeal the USA PATRIOT Act, which expanded government surveillance authorities. Restoring pre-2001 law directly and substantially increases privacy protections by removing those surveillance powers.
The bill contains no labor, union, or workplace provisions.
No religious liberty or anti-discrimination provisions are present.
